newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said the Commission, during its weekly meeting on Wednesday, had adopted a communication proposing to benchmark the competitiveness of European industry, the report on the employment in Europe in 1996, an interim report on transit and a report on the development of relations between the EU and Turkey. On this subject, van der Pas said the political relations were still difficult due to the human rights situation in Turkey.
Van der Pas also said the Commission had discussed its work programme for 1997 to be adopted by the European Parliament. He said the Commission should focus on political priorities.
The Commission discussed and issued a declaration on worrying situation of human rights, especially women's rights, in Afghanistan, he added.

Spokeswoman Sarah Lambert said there would be a technical briefing on the trans-european networks on Friday at 1215/1015 GMT, hold by officials from DGVII (Transport). Lambert said discussions would focus on the Kinnock Group's first meeting to be held on Friday.

In answer to a question, Van der Pas confirmed contacts between the Commission and the Spanish authorities on difficulties related to last year's Spanish budget but said no agreement had been reached yet.

Asked which countries were concerned by the Russian quotas on the import of vodka, announced to be introduced on 1st January 1997, spokesman Nicolaas Wegter said that Belgium was the premier European vodka exporter to Russia and that EU exported, during 1995, 200 million litres of vodka to Russia.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/911: The Commission asked the Russian authorities not to limit vodka and ethyl alcohol imports.
- IP/96/912: The European Commission calls for the respect of the rights of Afghan women.
- IP/96/915: Commission given go-ahead to negotiate new steel trade agreements with Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan.
- IP/96/916: Commissioner Wulf-Mathies citicizes EP's budgetary committee's vote on peace initiative.
- IP/96/917: Commission approves acquisition of Immuno by Baxter.
- Speech/96/241: Speech by Commissioner Cresson at the Space meeting.
- Speech/96/242: Speech by Commission President Santer at the French Institute for International Relations (IFRI).
- Speech/96/243: Speech by Commissioner Marin on the presence of the European Union in Latin America.
- Note on the preparation of the Fisheries Council of October 14 in Luxembourg.
- Business and consumers surveys, September 1996-No 9.
- POP IV Fourth multiannual guidance programme for the fisheries sector.
- Report on development in relations with Turkey since the entry into force of the customs union.
- Eurostat news release No 66/96: Slower growth in intra-EU trade.
- Eurostat, statistics in focus No1996-3: European patent applications.
